The cancer warning rule for coal tar hair dyes applies if the product contains an ingredient listed in 21 CFR 740.18(b), which includes 2,4-diaminoanisole (4-methoxy-m-phenylenediamine) and its sulfate salt (2,4-diaminoanisole sulfate). Since the formulation contains 2,4-diaminoanisole sulfate, it falls under the scope of the rule. The warning must appear on the principal display panel in a conspicuous and readable format as required by §740.2(a), unless an exemption is established under §740.2(b) due to label size limitations.

21 CFR 740.18(a)[1]: The principal display panel of the label must bear the warning: "Warning—Contains an ingredient that can penetrate your skin and has been determined to cause cancer in laboratory animals."  
21 CFR 740.18(a)[2]: This is the specific text of the required cancer warning for coal tar hair dyes containing ingredients listed in paragraph (b).  
21 CFR 740.18(b)[3]: Hair dyes containing 4-methoxy-m-phenylenediamine (2,4-diaminoanisole) or its sulfate salt (2,4-diaminoanisole sulfate) must comply with the requirements of this section; thus, the product in question is subject to the warning requirement.  
21 CFR 740.2(a)[4]: The warning statement shall appear prominently and conspicuously on the label, in bold type on a contrasting background, with letters and numbers not less than 1/16 inch in height, unless an exemption under paragraph (b) is established.  
21 CFR 740.2(b)[5]: If the label is too small to accommodate the warning, the Commissioner may establish an acceptable alternative method, such as smaller type size, by regulation; however, this requires a petition submitted to the Dockets Management Staff for approval.
